texts: good. the illness is recorded as a past state of Bevin Coombe, dated to the night of day 111 of Year 1, and also flat ("Bevin Coombe was ill") so a plain question about it still answers. One thing to know, not fixable by rewording: the day number goes into the same slot a day-of-month would use, so nothing downstream marks 111 as a day-of-year.
good. the tending, the Stilllight Lantern, "that night" resolved onto day 111 of Year 1, and "in place of Bevin Coombe" (recorded as Halden acting on Bevin's behalf) are all covered.
good. "substitute Keeper" is kept as one kind with keeper as its genus, and the whole claim is wrapped as past.

good. the refill, the mire-essence and its link to the Stilllight Lantern, and the past marking all land. One caveat no rewording fixes: midnight is stored here as hour 0, while the companion Lantern-night episode stored the same word as a bare "midnight" constant, so a question about midnight may not join the two episodes.

good. the wick is linked to the Stilllight Lantern as a part of it, and the carbonizing is recorded as a past event that affected the wick — the translator reads "was V-ed" as a passive verb, so there is no flat "the wick is carbonized" property beside it.
good. the denial covers the whole trimming — Halden, the wick and the past tense — while the wick itself stays asserted outside the denial.

good. the burning, the lantern, the past and the three-hour duration all land, and the dimness attaches to the burning rather than to the lantern, which matches your own later phrase "the dim burning".
good. the mist-light gets its own referent carrying "weak", with light as its genus, plus the three-hour duration and the past.

mixed: the Council's verdict is recorded with its content sealed, so the equivalence is not asserted as a fact of the world — right for a report of a judgment — but the embedded clause's past tense is dropped inside the seal, so nothing inside the verdict is dated. The wording itself is already the shape the translator handles, so this is a slip rather than a phrasing problem. If you intend the ruling to stand as a world rule rather than a one-off finding, the safer form is: "The Council judged that the dim burning is equivalent to an untended night."
